title: K8s Autoscaling Workshop — Knowledge Check
description: Validate that you understood how Dynatrace finds mis-sized Kubernetes workloads and how their requests are right-sized.
imagine: You right-sized the otel-demo-light workloads with Smartscape, DQL and a Workflow.
yourGoal: Show you understood what requests are, how the recommendations are computed and how they reach the cluster.

questions.title: What a request is
questions.content: What does a container's resource **request** decide in Kubernetes?

options.text: How much CPU and memory the scheduler reserves for the pod on a node
options.explanation: Placement and packing are based on requests, not on actual usage.

options.text: The most the container may ever use
How often the container is restarted
options.explanation: Requests have nothing to do with restarts.

questions.explanation: Requests are reservations: they decide where pods fit, whatever the pods really use.

questions.title: Opt-in
questions.content: Which workloads does the Smart K8s Resource Optimizer change?

options.explanation: The annotation is read from Smartscape; everything else is skipped.
System and other namespaces are never touched.

options.text: Only workloads with a CPU limit
options.explanation: Limits are not the selection criterion.

questions.explanation: The annotation is the opt-in: no annotation, no change.

questions.title: The formula
questions.content: How does the optimizer compute a new request?

options.text: p95 of the observed usage over 7 days, times 1.30
The average usage of the last hour
options.explanation: Too short and too low — spikes would be cut off.

questions.title: Where the data comes from
questions.content: Which data source gives the optimizer the containers' **requests**?

options.text: The ActiveGate's Kubernetes monitoring, via the Dynatrace Operator
options.explanation: Requests are Kubernetes object data read from the API.

options.text: The OpenTelemetry SDK in each service
options.explanation: SDKs report application telemetry, not pod specs.

questions.explanation: The Operator's ActiveGate feeds Smartscape and the container metrics.
hints: Which component talks to the Kubernetes API?

questions.title: Applying the change
questions.content: In this workshop, how do the recommendations reach the cluster?

options.text: applyRecommendations patches the workloads' requests with kubectl, and Kubernetes rolls the pods
options.explanation: An in-place apply instead of the upstream pull request.

options.text: The workflow pushes a commit to a GitHub fork
options.explanation: That was the original workshop; here no fork is needed.

options.text: The OpenTelemetry Collector rewrites the pods

questions.explanation: A rolling update replaces the pods with the new requests.
hints: What did you run in step 5?

learningObjectives: Explain what a resource request decides
Explain how the optimizer selects workloads and computes requests
Apply recommendations to a cluster and verify them in Dynatrace
